newsitem.title: USA: SunRiver sees profit in first half of 97.
newsitem.headline: SunRiver sees profit in first half of 97.

text.p: SunRiver Corp said Monday it expected to return to profitability in 1997 -- maybe as early as the first half of the year.
The company reported a loss of $11.7 million for 1996 after charges compared to a profit of $168,000 the previous year.

A supplier of text terminals and network computers, it said the loss was primarily due to a $9.7-million or $0.21-per-share loss in operating losses and write-offs at its discontinued TradeWave operation.
"We expect the company to return to profitable operations during 1997, potentially as early as the first half of the year," it said.
The company said it would announce a new range of network computer models in the spring with plans to begin early deliveries of the first model in the second quarter.
It also said it had negotiated new covenants with its commercial banks with the belief that it will remain in compliance with them.

"The company has no plans for additional financing activities such as those undertaken in 1995 and 1996," it said. "We have already begun the process of paying down debt, and will continue on that road in 1997, using a portion of our positive cash flow."
